substantive_reconstruction.carrier_and_convexity: I reconstructed the matrix carrier before using the geometric language. Over C, writing an arbitrary matrix as B+iC with B,C Hermitian shows that real nonnegative quadratic forms force every quadratic form of C to vanish; polarization gives C=0. Thus positivity already entails Hermiticity and the explicit Herm_d carrier does not add a state hypothesis. Herm_d is a REAL d^2-dimensional space, and for d>=1 trace one cuts out a real affine hyperplane A_d of dimension d^2-1. All finite-dimensional norms induce the same topology. For a probability mixture, each quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative terms with nonnegative coefficients; unit sum is unused there. Trace linearity instead gives sum_i p_i and needs that sum to be one, not coefficient signs. This separates proof roles without false individual necessity: (2,-1) on equal states still yields that state, whereas on orthogonal pure states in d>=2 it violates positivity despite trace one.
substantive_reconstruction.both_extremality_directions: For a positive trace-one matrix, spectral eigenvalues are nonnegative and sum to one. Rank one therefore gives exactly a unit-vector projector. Rank at least two supplies orthonormal positive-eigenvalue directions u,v; adding and subtracting t(P_u-P_v), with t smaller than both eigenvalues, creates two distinct positive trace-one matrices with midpoint rho. Thus higher rank is not extreme. Conversely, if P=s sigma+(1-s)tau with 0<s<1, every vector z perpendicular to its unit range vector has zero expectation in P. Positivity and the strictly positive mixture weights force zero expectations in sigma and tau separately. Spectral decomposition makes this equivalent to sigma z=tau z=0. Hermiticity then confines both ranges to the same one-dimensional support, and trace one forces sigma=tau=P. This proves the reverse implication rather than merely quoting the source's pure-state terminology.
substantive_reconstruction.affine_hull_and_relative_boundary: The PSD cone is closed because nonnegative quadratic forms are closed conditions, and trace one is closed. If rho is positive definite, an operator-norm-small Hermitian trace-zero perturbation E satisfies <v,(rho+E)v> >= (lambda_min(rho)-||E||)||v||^2, so it stays positive for ||E||<lambda_min. This is a neighborhood in A_d, not in the full matrix space. Applied at I_d/d it shows every trace-zero Hermitian direction has small positive and negative translates inside D_d, proving its REAL affine hull is A_d. Conversely, for a singular state in d>=2 choose a unit kernel vector z and unit w perpendicular to it. E_t=t(P_w-P_z) is trace zero, tends to zero, and gives expectation -t on z. Nearby points of A_d therefore lie outside D_d. Closedness proves every singular state is relatively boundary; positive-definite states are precisely the relative interior. Approaching any state by mixing with epsilon I_d/d also confirms closure of that interior.
substantive_reconstruction.dimensions_and_full_ambient_topologies: For d=1, A_1=D_1 is a singleton: it is relatively open in itself and has empty relative boundary, although its state is pure and extreme. For d=2 the only singular trace-one positive spectra are (1,0), so relative boundary equals pure states only in this special case. For d>=3, diag(1/2,1/2,0,...) is mixed, rank two and nonextreme, but singular and relatively boundary. Its trace-one perturbations diag(1/2+t,1/2,-t,...) explicitly leave positivity and converge to it. In the FULL Hermitian space, arbitrarily small nonzero rho+tI violate trace one; no state is interior. D_d is closed there, so its boundary is all of D_d. Hermiticity itself is a closed condition in M_d(C), hence D_d is closed in that larger usual real norm topology too; the same trace-violating perturbation again gives empty interior and the same full boundary. This includes mixed positive-definite states for d>=2 and avoids equating topology with convex extremality.
